header.title: Seven-Cs framework points to brand-level dispersion within luxury

s01_bottom_line.text: Goldman Sachs Research presents a seven-Cs benchmarking framework (clout, categories, consumer caliber, creativity, consistency, codes/icons, corporate) to differentiate long-term growth prospects across luxury brands and verticals.
The report offers the framework as a way to think about where the sector and individual makers may be headed, implying selectivity among brands and categories.
The framework implies returns within luxury depend on brand and category selection — bigger brands and higher-growth verticals (e.g. jewelry over beauty) — rather than uniform sector exposure.

items.text: Clout: bigger luxury brands secure better locations and enjoy lower rent as a percentage of sales ('big is beautiful').
Categories: some verticals such as jewelry have better growth potential than others such as beauty products.
The report offers a seven-Cs benchmarking framework to assess long-term growth drivers for the sector and individual luxury makers.
Consumer caliber: resilience of high-net-worth consumers makes high-end brands more resilient.
Corporate: many luxury-goods companies are partly owned and run by family members, a framework consideration.
